Lua addon authoring guide¶

This is the player-facing guide to writing Lua addons for the game. It covers how addons load, the callbacks you can implement, what the API lets you read and draw, how to save settings, feature detection, the sandbox rules, and — at the end — the adjustments existing addons need after the Phase 0/1 hardening.

For the exhaustive function-by-function list, see the Lua addon API reference. For the internals, see host internals.

Installing and enabling an addon¶

Addons are plain *.lua files in your game data Lua/ folder. Open it in-game with the addon manager's Open Folder button, or the /lua path chat command.

Newly added addons load disabled. After dropping a file in, open the addon manager and toggle it on (you will also see a "New Lua addon(s) detected and left disabled" line in chat). This is a safety change: a file you just downloaded does not run until you say so.

Reload all addons with /lua reload (or the manager's Reload All button). Unload them with /lua unload.

Addon metadata¶

The manager reads five optional fields from the top of your file. Declare them as locals with this exact form:

local ScriptName = "My HUD"
local Version = "1.0"
local CreatorName = "YourName"
local Description = "A heads-up display."
local IconPath = "icon.png"   -- relative to the Lua folder

The addon lifecycle and callbacks¶

Your addon is a script that defines global functions the game calls. Define only the ones you need.

Callback When it fires Arguments
ShroudOnStart() Once, when the addon loads or is enabled —
ShroudOnUpdate() Every frame —
ShroudOnGUI() Every IMGUI event (legacy drawing) —
ShroudOnConsoleInput(type, sourcePlayer, message) Each incoming chat line strings
ShroudOnExperienceGain(type, amount) On XP gain ("Adventurer"/"Producer") string, number
ShroudOnMouseOver(id, kind) / ShroudOnMouseOut(id, kind) Hover enter/exit of one of your widgets int, UI
ShroudOnMouseClick(id, kind) Click on one of your widgets int, UI
ShroudOnInputChange(id, text) Your input field changed int, string
ShroudOnToggleChange(id, isOn) Your toggle changed int, bool
ShroudOnSceneLoaded(sceneName) / ShroudOnSceneUnloaded() Scene transitions string / —
ShroudOnLogOut() At logout —
ShroudOnPlaySound(clipName) A UI sound played string
ShroudOnPlayFX(fxName, on) An FX started/stopped string, bool
ShroudOnPlayEmote(emote) You performed an emote via ShroudPlayEmote string
ShroudOnDisableScript() Your addon was turned off —

ShroudOnExperienceChanged is accepted as an alias of ShroudOnExperienceGain.

Declare everything local¶

All enabled addons share one global environment. A top-level function foo() or a bare x = 1 becomes a global that every other addon sees — and if two addons define a global with the same name, the last one loaded wins and quietly replaces the other's. Declare every helper and variable local. Only your ShroudOn* callbacks (and metadata fields the manager scrapes) need to be global-ish, and those are captured per addon at load time.

local state = {}                 -- good: private to this addon
local function refresh() ... end -- good

function ShroudOnUpdate()        -- callback: fine as a global
    refresh()
end

Reading game state¶

The API is read-mostly by design: you can read what your own UI already shows (your stats, your inventory, your party, your current target, whatever is under your cursor) and draw your own overlay, but there is no function to move, cast, target, loot, trade, or send chat. See the API reference for every read function.

Per-frame values (player position, health, focus, gold, time, mouse) arrive as globals such as ShroudPlayerCurrentHealth and ShroudMouseX, refreshed each frame. Everything else is a function call — call these only inside a callback (they are not registered yet at file top level).

Drawing UI¶

Two systems exist. Prefer the retained widget set (ShroudUIText, ShroudUIImage, ShroudUIButton, ShroudUIPanel, ShroudUIInput, ShroudUIToggle plus the ShroudSet* helpers): create objects once in ShroudOnStart, update them as needed. The legacy immediate-mode calls (ShroudGUILabel, ShroudButton, ShroudDrawTexture) run only inside ShroudOnGUI and will eventually be retired.

Hover tooltips on drawn icons (API v3)¶

An immediate-mode icon can tell the player what it is. ShroudDrawTextureTooltip(x, y, w, h, texId, text) draws a texture and shows text when the cursor is over it; ShroudGUITooltip(x, y, w, h, text) attaches a tooltip to a region you drew yourself. Combined with the real buff icon and native-matching tooltip text (ShroudGetBuffIcon(i) / ShroudGetBuffTooltip(i)), a buff-icon addon can show recognizable icons that name their skill on hover:

function ShroudOnGUI()
    for i = 0, ShroudGetBuffCount() - 1 do
        local tex = ShroudGetBuffIcon(i)
        if tex >= 0 then
            ShroudDrawTextureTooltip(40 + i * 44, 220, 40, 40, tex, ShroudGetBuffTooltip(i))
        end
    end
end

The Buff Icons reference addon is the full worked example.

Saving settings¶

Use the saved-variables API (see the reference): ShroudSetSavedVar(key, value) / ShroudGetSavedVar(key) persist per-character (or per-account) JSON to Lua/SavedVariables/<addon>.<scope>.json, written at logout and on demand. This replaces writing your own files with io.* — which is now confined to the Lua folder (see below).

Feature detection¶

New API is added behind a version number. Read ShroudLuaApiVersion (a plain global, safe at file top level) and gate accordingly:

local hasNewApi = ShroudLuaApiVersion and ShroudLuaApiVersion >= 3

The sandbox¶

Addons run inside a sandbox:

  • File access is confined to the Lua/ folder. io.open, os.remove, os.rename, and os.tmpname all work, but only for paths inside Lua/ (build them from the ShroudLuaPath global). A path outside the folder raises a Lua error.
  • os.execute, os.exit, and os.getenv are disabled. os.execute and os.exit raise a Lua error; os.getenv returns nil.
  • A runaway addon is stopped. If a single callback runs too long (an accidental infinite loop), it is aborted with an error rather than freezing the client. An addon that errors repeatedly in a short window is automatically disabled — fix it and /lua reload to retry.

Errors are reported in chat, prefixed with your addon's name.

Migrating an existing addon (Phase 0/1 changes)¶

Most addons need no changes. The list below is everything that changed; search your scripts for the named functions.

If your addon… What changed What to do
calls os.execute, os.exit, or os.getenv These now raise an error / return nil. Remove them. There is no supported replacement — they were never intended to be available.
reads or writes files outside the Lua/ folder with io.* / os.remove / os.rename Now raises a Lua error. Move the file inside the Lua/ folder; build paths from ShroudLuaPath. In-folder access is unchanged.
saves its settings by writing a file Still works if the file is inside Lua/. Prefer the new ShroudSetSavedVar/ShroudGetSavedVar API.
does heavy work in one callback A callback that runs too long is aborted. Spread work across frames, or use ShroudRegisterPeriodic. The budget is generous; only true hangs trip it.
relies on being auto-enabled when dropped in New addons now load disabled. Enable it once in the addon manager after installing.
defines ShroudOnPlayEmote This callback now actually fires (it never used to). Confirm the handler does what you intend.
throws errors every frame The addon is now auto-disabled after repeated errors. Fix the error; /lua reload to retry.
used /lua <function> from chat and found it did nothing /lua <func> [args] now correctly calls the named global; /lua code <lua> runs a snippet. Only globals from enabled addons are reachable — a disabled addon contributes nothing to call. Enable the addon in the manager first if you drive it through /lua <func>.
defined a top-level global helper that collided with another addon Unchanged behavior, but worth fixing. Make your helpers local (see above).

Everything else — the entire Shroud* read/UI/sound/periodic surface — keeps identical names, signatures, and return values, including long-standing quirks (0-based widget ids vs 1-based sound ids, the ShroudSetDragguable spelling, ShroudGetGameTime day/month being engine value +1, ShroudSetParent returning -1). Those are frozen for compatibility and documented in the API reference.

Sharing addons: the Community Addons window¶

You can share an addon with other players through the in-game Community Addons window (open it with the /addons chat command, or the Get Addons button in the addon manager). The window lists addons other players have submitted and an admin has approved. Each entry shows the author, a short description, how many players have it installed, and when it was last updated.

  • Install / Update / Remove download an approved addon into its own folder and, for updates, replace it in place. An installed addon starts disabled, the same as a file you drop in yourself — enable it in the manager (or with the window's Run toggle) once you have looked at what it does.
  • Removing an addon deletes its folder but keeps its saved variables, so reinstalling later keeps your settings.
  • Every version is read by an automated reviewer and then approved by a human before it appears in the list. The reviewer writes the one-paragraph description you see on each entry.

Packages vs. flat files¶

A shared addon is a package: a small zip containing a manifest.json, one or more *.lua files, and an optional icon.png and README.md. It installs into its own subfolder, Lua/<slug>/, instead of sitting loose in Lua/. The <slug> is a short lowercase id (letters, digits, hyphens) that uniquely names the addon in the store.

Your hand-installed flat *.lua files keep working exactly as before — the loader reads both loose files in Lua/ and one level of Lua/<slug>/ package folders. Inside a package, all the .lua files listed in the manifest run in the order listed and share one global environment (the same as putting several function definitions in one file); require() between package files is not supported.

The manifest.json for a package looks like this (the store builds it for you when you submit, so you rarely write it by hand):

{
  "manifest_version": 1,
  "slug": "loot-tracker",
  "name": "Loot Tracker",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "description": "Shows a running total of loot picked up this session.",
  "author": "YourName",
  "files": ["main.lua"],
  "icon": "icon.png",
  "min_api_version": 2,
  "permissions": []
}

version is three numbers (N.N.N) and must go up every time you submit an update. permissions is reserved for future capability grants and must be empty today. min_api_version is the lowest ShroudLuaApiVersion your addon needs; a player on an older build can install it but cannot enable it until they update.

Submitting your own addon¶

From the Community Addons window, pick your addon under Your local addons (for a single-file addon) or select an installed package, and choose Submit to Community. The game bundles your .lua file (plus its icon, if you set IconPath) into a package, generates the manifest, and uploads it — you do not build the zip yourself.

  • You sign in with your game account (the same login you use to play); the password is used only to authorize the upload and is never stored.
  • On the first submission you pick the slug and starting version. For an update, the slug is fixed and you supply a higher version and a short changelog.
  • After you submit, the addon is scanned and waits for an admin to approve it. Track its state in the window's My Submissions tab: Scanning, Waiting for review, Approved, or Rejected (with the reviewer's note).

The reviewer reads your code to write the player-facing description and to check for anything misleading or unsafe. The client sandbox (below) is still the real safety boundary — review is an extra check and a way to keep the catalog readable, not a replacement for it.

From a flat addon to a package¶

If you previously shared a flat MyAddon.lua by hand and now submit it as package myaddon, the packaged copy is a new addon identity: it starts disabled and with empty saved variables (the game keys enable-state and saved variables on the package, not the old filename). Players re-enable it once. If you want to carry a player's old settings across, ship one-time import code that reads the old Lua/SavedVariables/MyAddon.*.json through the confined io API and copies the values in with ShroudSetSavedVar. The store never deletes or renames a player's loose files; if a package would collide with a loose file of the same name, the game asks the player before moving the loose file aside.
